claims.text: The room-temperature HfNbTaTiZr alloy has a BCC structure.
The cast/annealed HfNbTaTiZr alloy has a homogeneous microstructure.
Atomic-size and electronic mismatches produce localized lattice distortions in HfNbTaTiZr.
Heating enhances local lattice distortions in HfNbTaTiZr.
Heating increases anharmonic phonon interactions in HfNbTaTiZr.
Enhanced anharmonic lattice vibrations soften the HfNbTaTiZr lattice.
Anharmonic lattice vibrations and enhanced local distortions reduce the effective elastic modulus as temperature rises.
Anharmonic lattice vibrations and enhanced local distortions reduce yield strength as temperature rises.
Anharmonic lattice vibrations and enhanced local distortions reduce ultimate tensile strength as temperature rises.
High-temperature stress–strain behavior will become more nonlinear relative to its room-temperature behavior.
The effective elastic modulus will be lower at elevated temperature than at room temperature.
The yield strength will be lower at elevated temperature than at room temperature.
The thermal expansion response will deviate from a simple linear prediction as anharmonic effects become significant.
The thermal expansion coefficient may exhibit temperature-dependent nonlinearity or an inflection point.
At room temperature, lattice vibrations in HfNbTaTiZr are predominantly harmonic.
At room temperature, HfNbTaTiZr exhibits minimal local lattice distortion relative to the heated state.
The proposed mechanism should govern behavior from room temperature to approximately 1100 degrees Celsius provided oxidation and phase transformations do not dominate.
